checks.claim: C1 Claim and assumption fidelity (P:Jensen, C:d1-first-calibration, supplementary L_* consumers, G:upper free of first-moment constants)
checks.reason: P:Jensen proves E u >= 1 from the nonnegative even-order pairing integrals and S_0=1, then E u^2 >= (E u)^2. The implication liminf t^-kappa log E u >= ell implies liminf of the second moment >= 2 ell is stated for an arbitrary real ell, and taking ell=L_* is explicitly conditional. Recomputed C:d1-first-calibration. A single chain of length 2k has increment sum <= t, so the spatial bound applies with t/2. The ordered-simplex temporal pairing sum is P_k(Z t^(2-alpha0))^k/(2k)!, and P_k/(2k)! = 1/(2^k k!). This gives (Z K/2^(b+1))^k t^(beta k)/(k! k^(bk)) with b+1 = 3-alpha. So C_{1,*} = q(Z K)^(1/q)/2, and C_{2,*}/C_{1,*} = 2^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) > 2. The unconditional constant is kept, and L_* <= C_{1,*} is stated only under the lower-rate premise. The supplementary consumers R:higher-calibrations, R:static-holder-scope, R:planar-scope and R:three-endpoint-scope all state 2L_* <= constant only if the intended first-moment lower bound holds. T:first is quoted as printed with the normalization caveat. T:full-upper uses no first-moment constant, and no correction is adopted.

checks.claim: C2 Fixed-noise Green limit in P:mixed
checks.reason: At fixed positive noise widths the colored covariances and Gaussian moments are bounded and continuous. p_eta*G_s are positive measures of mass s that converge weakly. Products of weakly convergent finite measures, and their continuous linear pushforwards, converge weakly. The integrands are dominated by a finite moment constant times the product of time gaps, which is integrable on the bounded simplices. Dominated convergence applied to the mixed moments with two Green widths gives a common limit, hence L2 Cauchy. The eta limit is taken at fixed noise widths, before any noise limit, as in source pp.13-14 (author-13 image and source-excerpts). No singular kernel is evaluated pointwise.

checks.claim: C3 Equal-length import and unequal-chain deduction
checks.reason: Author Lemma 4.4 (author-30 image) gives, for every D in Pi_n with two equal-length chains on [0,t1]x[0,t2], a finite joint limit as all 2n vertex widths tend to zero, with gamma^0_{delta_j v delta_k} gamma_{eps_j+eps_k} factors. Remark 4.5 chains Lemma 4.4 to (4.4) to Lemma 2.4 to Theorem 4.1. With ctilde(j) = ctilde(r+j) = c(j), the covariance matrix of the colored evaluations is 1{same color} K_jl. Wick then gives a sum over Pi_r(c) of uncolored diagrams B_{D'} with coefficient one. A color self-paired on a chain occurs four times in the doubled product, so all three pairings of those four vertices are kept; the r=2 example K12K34+K13K24+K14K23 is correct. After reversal each B_{D'} is an initial-chain Lemma 4.4 diagram with permuted widths, so it has a limit b_{D'}. The finite sum Q gives E[Y_a Y_b] -> Q and ||Y_a-Y_b||^2 -> 0. In the original unequal product each color occurs exactly twice, so D is the only compatible pairing, and L1 convergence of the product gives the limit. The reversal s'_j = t-s_{m+1-j}, y'_j = x-y_{m+1-j} gives each chain its own root. rho is an involution, so D -> D^rev is a bijection. Even kernels absorb the sign change. Empty chains (Y_0=1) and odd totals are handled. No product rule for multiple Stratonovich integrals is assumed. The series passage uses L:vertex-crude and does not depend on the mixed expansion.

checks.claim: C4 Source fidelity of the Crouzeix-Palencia and Chen 2023 inputs
checks.reason: cp-01 shows (3): ||f(A)|| <= (1+sqrt2) sup over W(A) of |f| for bounded A on a complex Hilbert space. It follows from (2) through smooth convex Omega_n shrinking to the closure of W(A), so it covers f holomorphic near that closure. cp-02 gives the algebra A(Omega), and cp-05/06 give Theorem 6 (C_Omega <= 1+sqrt2) for bounded A in B(H). E:cp-input matches this. Every application is to a bounded operator on a finite-mode, finite-Hermite, finite-band space; no unbounded extension, Kato theorem or journal numbering is used. chen-2023-02 shows the closing sentence of Theorem 1.1, stating that the variations in (1.4) and (1.5) are finite. L:physical-spectral-energy cites that clause for (1.5), and no Corollary 1.2 is imported.

checks.claim: C5 Complex roots and scalar estimates (L:complex-phase, L:interval-complex)
checks.reason: Recomputed. L_lambda+t = A_kappa^(1/2)(1-zK)A_kappa^(1/2) with ||zK|| <= delta. The ordered difference A_lambda^(1/2)[(L_lambda+t)^-1 - A_kappa^-1] = A_lambda^(1/2)A_kappa^(-1/2)(1-zK)^-1 zK A_kappa^(-1/2) has factor norms 1, 1/(1-delta), |z| d kappa^(a-2) and 1/kappa. Substituting t = lambda^2 s turns the integral of t^(-1/2) kappa^(a-3) into lambda^(a-2) I_a. With delta <= pi/(8 I_a) and 1-delta >= 3/4 this gives ||Q-1|| <= 1/6, ||Q|| <= 7/6 and ||Q^-1|| <= 6/5. The adjoint branch gives the other two comparisons, so all four are <= 2. Taking rho=s gives |<Bu,u>| <= 2 d s^a, and s=0 is handled by a limit. Taking rho=lambda gives x+lambda^2 >= (1-delta)(s^2+lambda^2). Weighted AM-GM gives s^(2a) lambda^(2-2a) <= s^2+lambda^2, hence y^2 <= (1/3) lambda^2 (x+lambda^2) and x >= -lambda^2/4. Then |w| <= x+2 lambda^2, which gives |Im sqrt w| <= lambda. Small and large |w| regimes give |F_h| <= max(sqrt(3/2) lambda h, sqrt3) e^(lambda h). |w|/|w+lambda^2| <= 1+4/3 = 7/3. CP gives 3, 6(1+lambda h), 6. With root factors the block norms are 3, 12(1+lambda h), 12, 12, summing to (39+12 lambda h) e^(lambda h) <= 100 e^(2 lambda h). The block identifications G A^(1/2) = F_h L_lambda^(-1/2) A^(1/2) and -A^(-1/2) L G = -A^(-1/2) L_lambda^(1/2) H_h keep operator order. The propagator is the exponential of a bounded generator and is entire in z. L:interval-complex needs no selfadjointness of V.

checks.claim: C6 Gaussian spatial and color bounds
checks.reason: From int e^(-s|eta+xi|^2) mu(dxi) = int p_2s(x) e^(i eta x) Gamma(dx) <= int p_2s Gamma, evenness and physical positivity give the Gaussian comparison, valid with physical atoms such as delta_0. Integrating against e^(-rho^2 s) and using the radial mass mu(B_r) = r^alpha mu(B_1) gives R_alpha rho^(alpha-2), via int r^(alpha-1)/(1+r^2) = pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2)). The column sum, sum ||A^(-1/2) M_e f||^2 <= R rho^(alpha-2) ||f||^2, comes from Gaussian isometry and Plancherel. Finite mode sums are sub-sums. Band compression works because S_b A^-1 S_b <= A^-1. The new-color vacuum insertion is an orthogonal sum over modes. In the Fock sandwich, R R* = sum a_i* a_i = (k+1) on degree k+1, annihilation is the adjoint, and the result is 2 sqrt(N+1) sqrt(R) rho^(alpha/2-2). The constants do not depend on angular shape, number of modes or band. The unweighted multiplication bound uses v_eps and appears only at fixed smoothing.

checks.claim: C7 Fixed-split statement, ordinary coefficients and local cutoff
checks.reason: B_i = P S_b (sum_j g_ij M_e_ij) S_b P with N_i = 2k_i. Unused amplitudes are evaluated at zero. A zero-length clipped interval makes every positive-power coefficient vanish. Original labels are kept. The statement covers every r_i+q_i = 2k_i with k >= 1 and lambda = k/T. The coefficients are ordinary power-series coefficients in the same Gaussian fields. Color reflection gives the parity constraint, and there are prod(2k_i+1) <= 3^k splits. The finite-word lemma with N_i >= r_i, q_i keeps every selected word exactly, including lowering. The proof derives the explicit pre-absorption inequality E:split-before-absorption and then C_split from the operator definitions. No fixed-degree propagator is identified with the untruncated evolution.

checks.claim: C8 Common chronological partition and metric product
checks.reason: The background set A_r or A_q contains only colors used on that copy. At |z_i| = rho_i, D(t) = sum delta_a omega_i^(2-a) <= delta_a Lambda^(2-a) by superadditivity of x^(2-a). This is an operator inequality on the joint Hilbert space and needs no conditioning. The partition uses all clipped background endpoints in (0,T) and the cross insertion times; coincidences are Lebesgue-null. M <= 2|A|+m+1 <= 2k+1 <= 3k+1. Sum Lambda_j Delta tau = lambda T + sum omega_i |I_i^T| <= k + sum k_i <= 2k. So prod ||P_j|| <= 100^(3k+1) e^(4k) = M_k. The identity-map norm is q_j = max(1, Lambda_j/Lambda_{j+1}), because A_new^-1 <= (Lambda_old/Lambda_new)^2 A_old^-1. At a background cut, (lambda+R+E)/(lambda+R+S) <= 1+E/lambda <= prod_E(1+omega/lambda). q_0 = 1, insertion cuts give 1, and the final return at T is charged as an ending. Each I_i^T ends once, so prod q_j <= D_A, with no extra copy per segment. The bound is a deterministic operator inequality, so it holds for correlated inputs.

checks.claim: C9 Cross-vacuum subspaces, word product and Dyson cube
checks.reason: Z_S keeps unused cross colors in vacuum and used ones in first degree, with truncated background factors. P_j acts only on background colors and space, and I_j is the identity, so both preserve Z_S. J_i (i not in S) takes vacuum to degree 1 <= N_i = 2 and maps Z_S into Z_(S plus i). Its norm is computed by orthogonality of g_ij and the tensored column bound with arbitrary dependence on other colors, giving c_i = sigma_i sqrt(R) lambda^((alpha-2)/2) because Lambda >= lambda. W_A = I_M P_M B_(M-1) I_(M-1) ... B_1 I_1 P_1 I_0 is read rightmost first, uses each segment and identity once, and its domains match. This gives ||W_A v|| <= M_k D_A ||v|| prod c_i. The coefficient of prod y_i in variation of constants is one ordered insertion per cross color, summed over permutations with coefficient 1. The simplices D_pi tile the cube up to null diagonals, so Minkowski gives prod c_i h_i with no m! factor. Noncommuting operators, overlap, nesting and empty A or C are all covered. checks.json also reproduces the cube ordering to about 1e-17 on three overlapping layouts, as a diagnostic only.

checks.claim: C10 Normalized Cauchy integral and explicit constant
checks.reason: Normalized vector Cauchy with prod dtheta/(2 pi) of total mass 1 contributes only prod rho_i^(-r_i). Each copy is bounded separately; then Cauchy-Schwarz on the same Gaussian space with ||w||_{1/T} <= k ||w||_lambda and ||v||_lambda <= ||v||_{1/T} gives the factor k^2. The bound is k^2 M_k^2 D_Ar D_Aq prod_B rho^(-2k_i) prod_C (R sigma^2 h^2 lambda^(alpha-2)) ||v||^2. D_Ar D_Aq = prod_B (1+k_i/(lambda h_i))^(ell_i). rho_i^(-2k_i) = (sigma^2 d^2/delta^2)^(k_i) (h/k_i)^((4-alpha)k_i). With d^2 = 4(2k_i+1)R <= 12 k_i R this is (12 delta^-2)^(k_i) (R sigma^2 h^(4-alpha))^(k_i) k_i^(-(3-alpha)k_i), which is bounded by the same expression over (k_i!)^(3-alpha). M_k^2 = 100^(6k+2) e^(8k) <= (100^8 e^8)^k. C_split = 100^8 e^8 max(1, 12 delta^-2) depends only on alpha. In P:interval-coefficients the local weights are R h^beta (1+1/(lambda h)), R lambda^(alpha-2) h^(2-alpha0) and R^l h^(beta l)(1+l/(lambda h))^2/(l!)^nu. Their expansions have positive powers (beta, beta-1, p, beta l, beta l-1, beta l-2), so substituting h <= LT/i is monotone. This gives v_i and b_{i,l} with C^k R^k T^(beta k). The positive generating-product identity has no missing multinomial.

checks.claim: C11 Inventory product and full summation
checks.reason: At z = theta k^nu with theta = 1/4, the third singleton term is theta k i^-p because nu+alpha-2 = 1. The (1+Q_i) factors contribute at most C k^(1/p). For i <= k, (1+li/k)^2 <= 4^l and S_nu(x) <= e^(nu x^(1/nu)) give C k sum i^(-beta/nu), which is finite since beta > nu. For i > k, P_i <= theta; the singleton tail is theta k^(nu+1-beta)(...) = C k^(alpha0), and the higher tail is C k^(2nu+1-2beta) = C k^(2alpha0-1) <= Ck. The coefficient is then <= theta^-k k^(-nu k) e^(Ck) <= C^k/(k!)^nu, uniformly in inventory size and depth. Summing with zero order <= e and the series sum x^k/(k!)^nu <= e^(nu x^(1/nu)) gives e exp(C R^(1/nu) T^(beta/nu)). The odd coefficients vanish by reflection.

checks.claim: C12 Mode and band removal and uniformity
checks.reason: At fixed smoothing and inventory, multiplication on degrees <= n is bounded by 2 sqrt(n+1) sqrt(v_max). The creation tail is controlled by the omitted pointwise variances through dominated convergence, and the annihilation tail vanishes on finite-coordinate vectors. Density plus the uniform bound gives strong convergence, and closedness identifies the limit. S_b converges strongly and commutes with free evolution. Each fixed word converges by dominated time integration, and the entire majorant gives compact-amplitude convergence. v_max serves only for identification; the uniform bound involves only R_alpha and parameter constants. Source convergence for fixed Gamma is qualitative and adds no rate constant.

checks.claim: C13 Finite terminal-chain lemma and model identification
checks.reason: Recomputed the mass recursion M_n = int (T-s) M_(n-1)(s) ds, which gives T^(2n)/(2n)!. Generalized Holder gives ||prod W||_2 <= sqrt((2n-1)!!) V^(n/2). Mean-square continuity on finitely many open time cells gives strong measurability and Bochner integrability. Fubini plus differentiating the MGF gives coefficient one per unordered pairing, and the two ordered domains have terminal endpoints. Symmetrization leaves the integral unchanged, so no extra n! appears. The ratio test term is |r| sqrt(V) T^2/((2n+2) sqrt(2n+1)). In d=3, Green widths are handled by weak convergence with finite cut points as null sets. The interval field has covariance exactly K_J(s,r) Gamma_eps with bounded variance; K_J is not time-stationary, and the comparison precedes any reversal. terminal-checks reproduces 1/3 and 1/105 for a constant potential, as an auxiliary diagnostic only.

checks.claim: C14 Dyadic majorant, localization and scaled bound
checks.reason: The three shifted grids are nested because 3t is an integer. Choosing 3|s-r| < h_j <= 6|s-r| works since H_0 >= 6T. A segment shorter than h/3 meets at most one boundary of the union, so some grid interval contains both points and |s-r|^-alpha0 <= 6^alpha0 |I|^-alpha0. Counts: 3(T/h+2) per level, cumulative <= 6T/h_j + 6(j+1) <= 6T/h_j + 72T/h_j = 78T/h_j, so L = 78 and c = 6^alpha0. Localization: G_s*f_T = s on the cone, so C_s f_T = 1; chains ending in B_1 stay in the cone. Spatial stationarity gives the volume ratio (T+2)^d. Source (2.23)-(2.24) on author-13 gives gamma^0_delta <= |t|^-alpha0 <= K_infty. Monotone convergence over J inside positive finite-N Wick integrals includes self-pairs and unequal chains, with no infinite-depth field. Replacing Gamma by a^2 Gamma changes only R; the regularized series exists by L:terminal-wick and no unsmoothed convergence is assumed.

checks.claim: C15 Uniform geometric tails and moment estimate
checks.reason: Nonnegative mixed moments give r^(2n) E|Y_n|^2 <= B_r, which passes to X_n through the fixed-order limit. Geometric tails are uniform in (eps, delta). Taking eps, delta to zero at fixed N and then N to infinity gives convergence of the full regularized solution. B(T;2) controls the tails and B(T;1) gives the final bound. The moment branch uses only Theorem 4.1 and CP, and is independent of P:mixed, L:crude-corrected and source Section 5. The mild branch separately uses L:vertex-crude. The five-stage trace (i)-(v) is consistent. Scope is d = 1,2,3, the full H:homog class including delta_0 at d = alpha = 1, with no first-moment constant.

Chen-Hu p.2145 states gamma >= 0, nonnegative definite with spectral measure, d = 1,2,3 and possibly generalized noise. p.2147 Theorem 1.2 states homogeneity with 0 < alpha < 2 and d, or alpha = d = 1, data (1,0) and the M functional. p.2152 states explicitly that the covariance may be generalized and gives the heat-regularized definition (2.18), and (2.17)/(2.19)-(2.22) give the product/measure conventions on pp.2151-2153. p.2165 gives Theorem 3.8(i), p.2173 the scaling (5.1), p.2175 the Chen 2023 finiteness interface (2^(alpha/(4-alpha)) M), and p.2180 gives (5.15). A nonnegative even PD tempered Radon covariance fits this class directly. L:planar-static-input checks Dalang by dyadic ball growth, and Gamma_st is built with proved PD (line mixture and Gaussian mixture), not by weighting. P:three-transfer assumes endpoint PD explicitly. At p=2, Lambda_st = 2(2 sqrt(M_st)/(4-chi))^(4-chi) matches (5.15). The rate comes from (5.15), not Chen 2023, and finitely many initial coefficients are enlarged. No Riesz or angular restriction is introduced.

Each insertion of color i changes only that color's degree by +-1, and F_l preserve degrees, so the prefix degree is <= r_i(l) <= N_i. Hence P is the identity before and after each insertion, by induction from vacuum, and raising and lowering both survive; linearity extends this to finite sums and Bochner integrals. It is applied with one color (N=n) in P:static-phase-all-orders, with N_i = 2k_i on both copies in P:interval-coefficients, and to cross colors with the truncated background in X in L:fixed-split. The fresh-column equality and tensor bound hold. The P:mixed color indicator and the r=2 three-pairing example are correct, and repeated covariance adds no hypothesis. Separate real/imaginary rho choices, the adjoint root, the four ordered bounds and the four-block sum need no selfadjoint V. The metric polynomial has positive exponents, and enlarging L to at least 1 is harmless. author-section4.txt confirms Section 4 uses Theorem 3.1/Lemma A.1 only at fixed Laplace parameters (theta = 1); (4.4) is a regularization limit distinct from (5.4). The finite-word screen supports this and is not a proof.

Author-14/15 show that Theorem 3.1 permits per-edge finite mu_jk with gamma_jk >= 0 and temporal sets A_jk, with nonnegative kernel functions G_l, a partition with #Q0 = #Q1 and #Q2 even, and a factor 2 on Q1. The per-edge measure e^(-(eps_j+eps_l)|xi|^2/2) mu is finite under (1.5), and A = [0, 1/(delta_j v delta_l)] matches (2.11). Green-smoothed e^(-theta r) p_eta*G_r are functions. N0 = theta^-2. N1 <= (A.1) at theta0, which decreases in theta (author-60/61). N2^2 <= (A.3) C theta^-2 for theta >= theta0, after enlarging to |s-r|^-alpha0 and removing the Gaussian multiplier as in (4.14). The weights telescope to e^(-theta s'_n) >= e^(-theta t). Then theta = theta0 + n/t and P_n n^-2n <= 2^n/n! give q_n(t) = e^(theta0 t) C^(n/2) t^n/sqrt(n!). The sum of sqrt(n+1) q_n converges by the ratio sqrt(C) T sqrt(n+2)/(n+1). The Green limit is taken before the noise limit, and Theorem 4.1 (author-22, vertexwise eps, delta) passes the bound to X_n. The constants depend on the fixed covariance and do not enter T:full-upper. No all-time (5.3)/(5.4) uniformity is claimed.

Source (2.12) (author-09) requires an L2 limit independent of how eps and delta tend to zero, and Definition 2.1 (author-10) requires Psi = G u 1_[0,t] to be integrable with (2.1). The closed space P_<=n contains the Bochner terms and X_n. The occupied bound ||HF|| <= (sqrt(n+1)+sqrt(n)) ||H|| ||F|| follows from normalized Hermite raising and lowering with H as the first basis vector, so F may depend on H; it extends by closedness. mild-multiplication-screen's negative control (3 vs 1) shows a vacuum bound would fail. Joint stationarity gives y-uniform approximation and continuous L2 representatives. At fixed a, multiplication by W_a keeps the inner L2 convergence, with domination 2 sqrt(n) sqrt(V_a) q_(n-1)(T) and Green mass t-s; this gives I_(n,a) as the inner limit, exact for n=1. Joint Theorem 4.1 convergence then gives I_(n,a) -> X_n via the zeta/r argument. The mixed-vertex bound sup_a ||I_(n,a)|| <= q_n gives tails uniform in a. V_a appears only for fixed-a product existence. In d=3, eta-first limits use continuous bounded vector functions, partitions of unity, tightness and dominated time integration. W_a u and I_a = sum I_(n,a) follow from closedness and the summability of sqrt(n) q_(n-1). Taking a to zero then N to infinity gives the mild equation. No uniqueness or Section 5(ii) proof is imported, and P:mixed's use of this branch is not circular.

minor: L:physical-spectral-energy: the step from Chen 2023 Thm 1.1 finiteness of the (1.5) variation to Q(f) <= (1/2)||f||^2||grad f||^2 + C0||f||^4 relies on quartic homogeneity Q(cf) = c^4 Q(f) applied to f/||f||. The text compresses this to 'restricted ... and then normalized'. One explicit line would help. The step is correct.

P:mild-construction, d=3: Definition 2.1/(2.12) is applied to a measure-valued random integrand with the Green-width limit taken before the noise limit. This extends the source's deterministic convention (Remark 2.3, pp.13-14). The manuscript states the choice explicitly; a one-sentence note that this is the adopted reading of the source definition would help.

P:mild-construction and L:vertex-crude: joint (s,y) strong measurability of positive-width terminal integrals, and of X_(n-1)(s,y) through countable-width pointwise limits, is asserted briefly. It is standard but not spelled out.
L:vertex-crude: the absorption of Theorem 3.1's factor 2 on Q1 and of the C0 powers into C_1^n is left implicit ('exactly as in theta-envelope'). It is valid since #Q1 + #Q2 <= 2n.

P:interval-coefficients: the split-count wording ('2m_i+c_i <= 3(m_i+c_i)' together with 'the same split-counting factor already absorbed ... not a second charge') is confusing. The product of (2k_i+1) <= 3^k is charged once, which suffices.

Notation overload that could mislead a cold reader: q_n(t) (crude envelope), q_j (metric ratio), q = 3-alpha; a for widths versus a = alpha/2; delta_a versus delta widths; c (inventory) versus c_i (column constants); Gamma as a measure versus Euler Gamma. The authors flag only the last.
